svg.aria-label: How to write സ ് ക: 3 parts, സ, ്, ക, one after another
svg.title: Writing സ ് ക
svg.desc: 3 parts written one after another: സ, ്, ക (malayalam). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: സ: SPACE Kerala (Melwin Sunny and Shaiju T), Thooval Malayalam alphabet learning tool, formation arrows for സ in data/SA.png: green start, blue turn, red end (GPL-3.0, 2013) <https://github.com/spacekerala/Thooval/blob/87143b560bf5aab43837d9da2cddab9bd59cd391/data/SA.png>; ്: Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026), js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ്, drawn alone; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0 <https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree/blob/e0c9d57dd32031c948da4d5f8432aae3e22c5bba/js/src/stroke-data.raw.json>; ക: Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table IV 'How to Write Consonant Symbols', p. xxv: movements 1-7 for ക, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-035.jpg>. Source notes on variation: സ: Thooval's SA.png starts at the foot of the left arch (green), climbs clockwise over it and runs down the stem to the line (blue turn), climbs the stem again, sweeps over the middle arch, down and round the bowl, and up to the top-right tip (red). Thooval is a GPL-3.0 teaching tool, so only these facts are cited; no image, path or template point is copied. It asks the learner to keep the pen down to the end of every letter, so its single run is checked against two recorded sources that could have shown a lift. Santhosh Thottingal's hand reference curves (gitlab.com/santhoshtr/hand, MIT, 2019), which keep several strokes where a glyph has them, record സ as one stroke from the lower left to the upper right. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 31 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the lower left (26 of 31) and end at the upper right (31 of 31). The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to Thooval's letterforms; the climb back up the stem retraces the ink just drawn. ്: Jayasree records the candrakkala drawn alone as one stroke: it starts at the left tip, dips round the bottom of the cup and rises to the right tip (start upper left, end upper right). This is the sign's own ductus only; where it goes against its carrier stays the compositionSource's claim, and no written order against a carrier is claimed. Jayasree keeps one recorded gesture per pen-down stroke, so one stroke means the recorder did not lift. Only these facts (stroke count, start, order, direction and end) are taken; no recorded coordinate is copied. The stroke data is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) as "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree; this record adapts it, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to the recording, which was drawn over the Manjari typeface. One recorder, so confidence is medium. ക: Moag's Table IV (p. xxv) starts on the left leg of the top loop at the height of the crossbar, climbs clockwise over the loop and down its right leg (1), rounds the bottom of the middle bowl to the left (2), climbs the middle stem (3), runs back down into the left bowl (4), rounds the left bowl up to the left end of the crossbar (5), draws the crossbar left to right (6) and curls the right-hand hook down to finish at the lower right (7). Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. Santhosh Thottingal's hand reference curves (gitlab.com/santhoshtr/hand, MIT, 2019), which keep several strokes where a glyph has them, record ക as one stroke from the upper centre to the lower right. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker; 105 of the 107 unique samples show no jump between consecutive points of the kind a lift makes, and they most often start at the upper left (49 of 107) and end at the lower centre (59 of 107). SPACE Kerala's Thooval (GPL-3.0, facts only) starts its KA.png at the middle centre and ends it at the lower right. Moag, Thooval and hand all start in the upper or middle centre and end at the lower right; grahyam is the outlier, and 2 of its 107 samples lift once. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to Moag's drawing; the run back down the middle stem retraces the ink just drawn.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 5 movements
Part 2 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 3 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 7 movements
Part 1: stroke order after SPACE Kerala (Melwin Sunny and Shaiju T), Thooval Malayalam alphabet learning tool, formation arrows for സ in data/SA.png: green start, blue turn, red end
Part 2: stroke order after Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026),
js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ്, drawn alone; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0
Part 3: stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC
BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table IV 'How to Write Consonant Symbols', p. xxv: movements 1-7 for ക, written by hand by Thomas Joseph
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
